newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude bullish, gasoline is key.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude bullish, gasoline is key.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - July 16 -------------
+NYMEX crude put in a strong showing on Tuesday and there is room for a move upwards. Gasoline is the key to the market.
+Expect resistance at $19.73, the 40-day moving average, and then at $20.00.

NYMEX crude oil futures are likely to stage a rally again on Tuesday although the market faces hurdles on the way up to $20.00 a barrel, technical analysts said on Wednesday. Gasoline is the key to the market.

August NYMEX crude gained 68 cents a barrel on Tuesday and closed at $19.67, while August gasoline soared 1.59 cents to end at 59.94 cents a gallon. NYMEX August heating oil gained 1.28 cents to close at 52.95.
"Technically the market, led by unleaded gasoline, has the potential to burst higher," said Charles Gray at Prudential Bache International in London.

"The rally looks good but may falter temporarily. Gasoline has broken a flag formation, with the implied target at 63.00," he said, referring to a candlestick pattern dating from the beginning of this month.

Analysts have also noted the 50 percent retracement of the move from the 64.40 cent high on May 16, formed on the August contract chart, and the 54.65 low on June 23. This retracement lies at 59.52 cents and this is likely to provide support for gasoline.
They also said 60.00 cents was an important psychyological number to watch for.
In addition, gasoline was trading on ACCESS above the 60.10 high of Tuesday's trade and an open above this level would create a gap, which would add another layer of support.
For WTI crude, Gray pointed to the 40-day moving average on the continuation chart at $19.73, just above current levels on ACCESS.
Above that the target of a current wedge formation lies at $20.00, followed by another resistance level at $20.38, the 50 percent retracement of the down move from May 16 to June 20.
This level also lies adjacent to a key falling trendline from January, which currently crosses the price action at $20.35, Gray said.
"Overall we are approaching a watershed for the market," he said, and warned: "If momentum is not maintained today early on we are vulnerable to a pullback, especially if Brent fails at $18.55."
He said one layer of support for August NYMEX crude lay at $19.34, the middle of the range of Tuesday's trade.
